findings.reason: The 1-count agreement is wrong in both places: total=1 renders the plural noun 'چیٹس' and shown=1 renders the plural verb 'دکھائی جا رہی ہیں'. The one-row result is a real state (sidebar-scope-paging.ts documents 'Showing 1 match of 120 chats'), and the UR CLDR categories are one/other. The two search variants render the denominator the same way and need the same one/other arm on total; their shown clause already pluralises correctly.

observations: Merged bytes are byte-identical to the branch parent d784571d90; six keys are new versus main (agents.builtin_offer, catalogue.total, catalogue.total_search, catalogue.total_search_clipped, groups.badge, section.current_chat). Key order equals English.

groups.badge: English uses # in both arms; Urdu uses an explicit {badge, number, ::group-off} in each arm. Rendered 0/1/2/1000 -> '0 چیٹس' / '1 چیٹ' / '2 چیٹس' / '1000 چیٹس'. The 1-count agreement is correct; ungrouped formatting matches the file's counters.

agents.builtin_offer: rendered count 0/1/2/6/7; spelled arms through six and a digit in other, matching the context contract; the one arm uses singular 'ایجنٹ … ہے' and 'اس میں', the plural arms 'ایجنٹس … ہیں' and 'ان میں'.

supersedes.why: The merged bytes no longer match the recorded pair; this receipt names the current bytes so ledger-assemble can move the old audit to superseded and bind the new one.

scope: All 49 keys at the merged bytes, read against the English source and the en context sidecar. The merged ur file is byte-identical to branch parent d784571d90 and adds six keys versus main.
method: Manual side-by-side read of every ur value against its en value and context; mechanical checks: key parity both directions and key order, ICU parse and normalised placeholder/select/plural/skeleton comparison with @formatjs, bidi-control and punctuation scan, byte hashes from git objects, and for the sidebar rendered outputs at counts 0/1/2/1000 with intl-messageformat. For the viewer, per-key union provenance against both merge parents.

exceptions: ui.chat.sidebar.groups.badge: en uses # in both plural arms; ur uses an explicit {badge, number, ::group-off} in each arm. Same value and arm structure; the number formatting is deliberately ungrouped and matches the file's counters.
icu.note: Normalised comparison: an en # inside a plural arm and an ur {arg, number, ::group-off} of that plural's own argument are the same value; the only such substitution is groups.badge. Executed with @formatjs/icu-messageformat-parser 3.5.21; output recorded in this receipt.
